notes: Shared by the API (pytest) and the portal (vitest); both parsers must agree on every row. Text is a comma-separated list of entries, each `ID[type][lag]`: an ID of ASCII digits (leading zeros allowed, so 03 is 3), an optional link type FS, SS, FF or SF (default FS) and an optional lag that starts with a sign (`+2d`, `-4h`, `+2 days`). Whitespace is allowed between the ID and the type and between the type and the lag, but not between the sign and the lag number. The type is case-insensitive for ASCII letters only: do not use a Unicode-aware match (no `u` flag), because U+017F (long s) folds to `s` there and `3ſs` must stay invalid, and `\d` must not match non-ASCII digits. Only ASCII whitespace (space, tab, CR, LF, FF, VT) is trimmed or allowed: a no-break space or any other Unicode space is invalid, so do not use String.trim() as is. The whole text is trimmed first and must then be at most 512 characters (whitespace around it is not counted); an empty or all-whitespace text is no links, `[]`. Split on the ASCII comma only (a fullwidth comma is not a separator) and trim each entry; an empty entry (`2,,3`, `2,`, `,2`) is invalid. The lag, trimmed, goes through the lag rules in durations.json with the day as the default unit, so its own limits apply (at most 64 characters, 9 integer digits) and a bare number is days. A lead is a negative lag. Entries are checked in order, and a self reference, an ID that is not in `valid_ids` and a repeated ID (03 repeats 3) are all invalid. Parse rows are [text, [[id, type, minutes, unit, elapsed], ...]] and the parsed list keeps the text order. Invalid rows are plain texts that must fail with valid_ids and self_id from this file. `ids` rows are [text, valid_ids, self_id, expected or null]. `sized` rows build the text as `outer` spaces + head + `inner` spaces + tail + `outer` spaces, and are [outer, head, inner, tail, expected or null]. Format rows are [[[id, type, minutes, unit, elapsed], ...], text]. Format joins entries with a bare comma. A zero lag is left out whatever its unit (the unit is not kept) and the link type is written only when it is not FS, so a zero-lag FS link is the ID alone (`3`) and a zero-lag SS link is `5SS`. Any other lag writes the type first, even FS (`3FS+2 days`). A lag that is not zero but rounds to zero in the two-decimal display is written with its own sign (`3FS+0 days`, `3FS-0 days`) so the text still parses; it reads back as a zero lag.
